title: Symfony Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Make a controller route
examples.description: A Route attribute maps a URL to a controller method. Open GET /hello.
examples.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/hello", methods: ["GET"])]
public function hello(): Response { return new Response("Hello, Asha!"); }
}

examples.title: Return JSON data
examples.description: JsonResponse turns an array into JSON and sets its content type. Open GET /book.
examples.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/book", methods: ["GET"])]
public function book(): JsonResponse { return new JsonResponse(["title" => "Moon Trip", "pages" => 24]); }
}

examples.title: Read a route value
examples.description: A route placeholder can become a method input. Open GET /hello/Ravi.
examples.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/hello/{name}", methods: ["GET"])]
public function hello(string $name): Response { return new Response("Hi, " . $name . "!", 200, ["Content-Type" => "text/plain"]); }
}

examples.title: Read query data
examples.description: A Request object gives access to query values. Open GET /search?q=cat.
examples.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/search", methods: ["GET"])]
public function search(Request $request): JsonResponse { return new JsonResponse(["term" => $request->query->get("q", "")]); }
}

examples.title: Constrain a path number
examples.description: A route requirement describes allowed path text. Open GET /double/4.
examples.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/double/{n}", requirements: ["n" => "[0-9]+"], methods: ["GET"])]
public function twice(int $n): JsonResponse { return new JsonResponse(["answer" => $n * 2]); }
}

examples.title: Read a JSON body
examples.description: Request::toArray reads JSON into an array. Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}.
examples.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/books", methods: ["POST"])]
public function create(Request $request): JsonResponse {
 $data = $request->toArray();
 if (!is_string($data["title"] ?? null)) return new JsonResponse(["error" => "Title needed"], 400);
 return new JsonResponse(["title" => $data["title"]], 201);
}
}

examples.title: Generate a named URL
examples.description: A route name lets code build a link without repeating its path. Open GET /link.
examples.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/hello/{name}", name: "hello", methods: ["GET"])]
public function hello(string $name): Response { return new Response($name); }
#[Route("/link", methods: ["GET"])]
public function link(): Response { return new Response($this->generateUrl("hello", ["name" => "Asha"])); }
}

examples.title: Return a redirect
examples.description: RedirectResponse tells a client where to request next. GET /start ends at /hello in a browser.
examples.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/start", methods: ["GET"])]
public function start(): RedirectResponse { return new RedirectResponse("/hello"); }
#[Route("/hello", methods: ["GET"])]
public function hello(): Response { return new Response("Welcome"); }
}

examples.title: Add reply metadata
examples.description: A Response has a header bag. Open GET /note and inspect Cache-Control.
examples.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/note", methods: ["GET"])]
public function note(): Response { $response = new Response("Practice note"); $response->headers->set("Cache-Control", "no-store"); return $response; }
}

examples.title: Restrict an HTTP method
examples.description: The methods option limits which requests match. GET /ready gives this reply; POST is not allowed.
examples.code:
<?php

use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/ready", methods: ["GET"])]
public function ready(): Response { return new Response("Ready"); }
}
